question: A beam of yellow helium-neon laser light has a wavelength of 550 nm in vacuum. As this light beam enters a slab of **Perspex (acrylic)** (refractive index n = 1.49), what is the new wavelength of the light INSIDE the Perspex (acrylic)?
wrong_answers_pool: 819.5 nm (multiplied wavelength by n instead of dividing)
550.0 nm (assumed wavelength does not change across boundary)
explanation: Light slows down in an optical medium: v = c / n. Frequency f remains constant. Therefore λ_medium = v / f = (c / n) / f = λ_vacuum / n = 550 nm / 1.49 = 369.1 nm.

tags.learning_outcome: Calculate compressed wavelength inside Perspex (acrylic)
